blocks.x: OpenAI is piloting brand suitability controls with DoubleVerify and Integral Ad Science, giving advertisers an independent read on how the ad safeguards in ChatGPT work, the company announced on Monday during Advertising Week New York.

The two verification firms will assess how OpenAI applies its brand safety standards in a controlled testing environment, without access to private user conversations. OpenAI says the goal is to give advertisers greater transparency into how those safeguards work while protecting conversation privacy.

Adweek notes that bringing in outside verification follows a path other platforms have taken to win over buyers wary of media sellers grading their own work, and that both firms already measure brand safety placements across TikTok, Meta and Reddit. The pilots here are narrower for now, and it is unclear whether either firm will measure placements in live campaigns.

OpenAI also launched Negative Phrases, which lets brands set placement exclusions specific to their own policies. The company confirmed it was testing the tool in August, after Adweek reported that advertisers were seeing ads misaligned with user conversations in ChatGPT.
Alongside this, OpenAI is testing a larger ad format led by images, which appears during image generation, and is expanding its roster of measurement partners.

blocks.cap: TikTok's announcement of its advertising updates.

blocks.x: At Advertising Week New York 2026, TikTok set out a package of agentic advertising and commerce updates spanning every stage of the customer journey.

On the selling side, TikTok says it is building new agentic commerce shopping experiences, starting with Buy Direct and Shopping Assistant, and building them with commerce and payment platforms including Salesforce, Shopify, Shoplazza and Stripe. Buy Direct is an in-app checkout that lets a shopper buy from a brand without leaving TikTok, in one click from the For You feed. Shopping Assistant is a conversational agent that handles product details, shipping, sizing, availability and purchase in a single conversation.
Agentic Leads is a separate agent for lead generation, running guided conversations in TikTok direct messages and in lead forms on advertisers' own websites.

On the buying side, TikTok is bringing its TikTok Ad Network to advertisers in the United States, extending campaigns across what it describes as a premium network of nearly 400,000 apps, and is opening Search Ads Campaign powered by Smart+ along with Smart+ Creative Selection, which gathers an advertiser's own assets, Symphony's generated creative and creator content into one approval workflow.

TikTok also says its business interface built on the open Model Context Protocol is now available as a connector across several platforms and registries, and that advertiser use of it for campaign activation has grown by more than 200%, citing its own internal data for July to September 2026.

blocks.x: Omnicom Media has partnered with the advertising platform Rembrand on what it calls a first to market capability that lets brands identify, plan and activate placements inside premium streaming content.

The pair plan to use Rembrand's VISTA platform, which uses AI to scan publisher content and identify scenes that can be monetized. Omnicom Media's Content Collective, its branded content unit, then works the placements into the content. The aim is to scale placement inside content beyond isolated instances.

Omnicom Media picks the shows for a brand using its RealID audience product within Acxiom, matched against viewership data from streamers, then maps that against the opportunities in VISTA. A packaged goods client could be inserted into an episode of a cooking reality show after it has been produced and shot. Digiday notes the idea is not new, but doing it after production is.

Digiday reports the holding company's media network is still negotiating with several media companies that run streaming services, and could not name any of them. Megan Pagliuca, chief product officer for North America, said this is the first time the capability has been used by the buy side, having historically been a sell side technology, and called it still a nascent capability.

Omnicom Media's own research with Rembrand, rather than an independent study, found that placements inside content paired with traditional video ads drove a 5.5 times increase in message recall and a fourfold increase in both purchase intent and perception of the brand as premium.

blocks.x: From Monday, Gap customers can discover items through two outside platforms. Alta Daily curates outfit suggestions from variables including a user's schedule, budget and the weather forecast, and can surface items from a shopper's existing wardrobe as well as brands' assortments. Daydream takes everyday language and returns fashion ideas, with access to all four Gap Inc. brands: Gap, Banana Republic, Old Navy and Athleta.
Old Navy and Banana Republic customers can describe what they are looking for in natural language to conversational shopping agents on those two brands' websites and apps.

Sven Gerjets, chief technology officer, says he is aware shoppers can be wary of or even disappointed by shopping experiences assisted by AI. Retail Dive cites a SmartCustomer survey last month finding 45% of purchases consumers regret making with AI help were apparel and footwear, and research from Synchrony and Oxford Economics finding consumers are more likely to shop with AI at retailers they already trust, but are wary of how their data is used.

Agentic media buying is all the rage, including for streaming TV. A new joint effort announced Tuesday will use custom agents to help brand marketers get more from their streaming TV investments, including upfront commitments. The initiative brings together NBCUniversal, its SSP FreeWheel, Dentsu-owned agency Carat and agentic analytics platform Newton.

Custom buying agents pair identity data from NBCU and FreeWheel with audience intelligence from Dentsu and Newton. The agent uses that audience data and ad performance data to recommend NBCU ad inventory based on an advertiser's desired outcome.

An unnamed luxury retailer working with Carat is the first marketer to use the solution, although the joint offering will eventually be available to all Dentsu clients. In the meantime, Carat is busy building custom agents for specific advertiser KPIs, everything from search lift to incremental reach.

The promise is that agents could bring outcomes-based buying closer to the mainstream in CTV. But if every buy is judged by immediate results, advertisers could end up sacrificing long-term brand building for short-term gains.

blocks.x: TrafficGuard, the ad verification platform owned by Adveritas Ltd, said an analysis of 40,021 clicks on OpenAI's ChatGPT ads found invalid rates between 0.1% and 34% depending on the advertiser, with four hosting and proxy networks behind 47% of the flagged clicks.

TrafficGuard's figures count clicks that reached advertisers' websites, not clicks billed by OpenAI, and the company sells click verification, so the findings come from a party with a commercial interest.

Placement guardrails assess whether a conversation is appropriate for advertising, and Negative Phrases are now available to qualifying advertisers that need exclusions specific to their own policies.

The pilot would have independent partners assess OpenAI's suitability policies and guardrails without accessing private user conversations; OpenAI names Integral Ad Science in a parallel pilot.

When former MullenLowe U.S. CEO Frank Cartagena launched his own creative shop, OK Future, he wanted to test how much generative AI would let his agency of four people punch above its weight.

Its first work, Goodwipes’ “Meet Asstra,” a spoof of OpenAI’s commercial for its AI model Astra, went from concept to execution in four days with generative AI tools and curbed the projected $700,000 production costs. A minute-long produced commercial typically takes about six weeks, he said.

Goodwipes and OK Future handled the script, character building, storyboarding and edits; tools including ArtCraft, Seedance and OpenAI’s Astra visualized and voiced the characters and produced the location.

The team worked in shifts around the clock on little sleep. “I really wouldn’t recommend that this be the norm of a project. It’s just an unsustainable pace,” Cartagena said. “It’s a total pressure cooker.”
The spot drove more than 750,000 Reddit views in its first 48 hours and has since reached almost 1.5 million views across subreddits, with more than 800 shares, according to a company spokesperson.
Advancements in AI are helping Walmart save money, which it is, in turn, reinvesting in customer experience improvements, according to U.S. CEO David Guggina.

“We have been leaning into AI for quite some time — we've had physical AI in our supply chain for over seven years — and you can see it reshaping our company, reshaping our customer value proposition,” Guggina said in a conversation with Goldman Sachs’ Katharine McShane.

The gains show most in e-commerce: sales grew 24% year over year in Q2, the 10th consecutive quarter of more than 20% growth. Guggina credited AI-driven efficiencies — faster delivery and cost savings — that were reinvested into competitive pricing and customer experience.

Sparky, which Guggina describes as “becoming more and more capable,” is central to those improvements. Weekly engagement with Sparky has grown 60% quarter over quarter, and its new visual search has led to a 57% spike in conversion compared with text-based searches.

Guggina is also “really happy” with partnerships with external AI agents like OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Google’s Gemini, which most often deep link customers to Walmart with “fantastic conversion rates.” That contrasts with Amazon, which last month moved to block Meta’s new AI assistant Muse from its site. Many customers arriving via ChatGPT and Gemini are new or returning, with a “very high” organic repeat rate.

blocks.x: Ads Uploader, a bulk ad-submission platform for Meta, published September 2026 figures showing that AI agents connected directly to the service accounted for 17.5% of the 36,289 batches submitted through it, according to the company.

Applied to the total, that share works out to about 6,350 agent batches over the month, or roughly 212 a day on a 30-day window. The same release puts the month's output at 286,137 Meta ads, about 9,500 a day.

A batch counts as agent-made when an AI agent submits it through the platform's MCP server or its command-line interface. The definition is based on the channel, not on the degree of autonomy, and the release does not split supervised from unsupervised batches.
"A lot of advertisers already have an agent doing the setup work," said Chris Pollard, founder of Ads Uploader. "Last month about 1 in 6 batch launches on our platform came from one."
The data is supplied by the vendor, covers a single month and a single ad platform, and has not been audited. The figures arrive as Meta, Amazon and X open their own ad systems to agents.

OpenAI has launched a virtual try-on feature for ChatGPT users. When users browse clothing and accessories on ChatGPT, they can click the “try on” button, take or upload an image of themselves and then generate images of themselves wearing those products.
Shoppers can save products to Favorites or make a folder in their ChatGPT Library. The features are available on ChatGPT's website and mobile app.

As OpenAI adds shopping features, more retailers are experimenting with the platform: David's Bridal set up shop on Shopify's Agentic Storefronts for ChatGPT in April, and Etsy debuted its ChatGPT app in May.

With try-on, OpenAI is catching up to Google, which debuted virtual try-on for women's tops in 2023, then extended it to dresses and shoes. A 2024 Perfect Corp. survey found brands using virtual try-on saw sales conversion rates more than double.
Google Ads now lets you preview the assets generated by Google AI for your Google Ads AI Max campaigns, in a new “Text customization asset previews” section of the Search campaigns help page.

“Use asset previews to view sample text assets generated by Google AI for your campaign… to see whether generated text assets conform to your defined brand and text guidelines before you opt in to text customization or launch a new campaign.”

blocks.x: Pinterest has introduced Beauty Guides, a new AI-based feature. It turns hair and nail Pins into personalized, actionable guides, helping people actually recreate the styles they discover on Pinterest.

Pinterest's visual recognition technology analyzes the hairstyle, color, nail shape, finish and other details in a Pin, and a large language model (LLM) organizes them into what to ask for at the salon, the process, similar styles, related products and step-by-step instructions. Users open a hair or nail Pin in close-up and tap 'Get the Guide.'

Matt Madrigal, chief product and technology officer (CPTO), said, "People come to Pinterest with a clear point of view, even when they can't put the style they want into words." The feature is one example of 'Pinterest Intelligence,' which combines first-party data, visual recognition and purpose-built AI models.

More than 85% of Pinterest users said they discover new beauty trends on Pinterest before anywhere else. Beauty Guides is rolling out first to iOS users in the U.S., with plans to expand to more regions and product categories.

Most of eHealth's customers call during Medicare's roughly 54-day open enrollment window, about half a million calls, and 70% to 80% buy by phone, which left some waiting six hours for a licensed agent.

The health insurance agency now uses Regal's LLM-based voice agent, Alice, to prescreen callers. According to data Regal provided to CX Dive, Alice answers every call immediately, earns 77% "exceptional" satisfaction ratings and has a 27% higher purchase rate than eHealth had with human screeners from an outsourced call center.

The deployment began in February 2025 as an after-hours pilot. Because regulations require an uninterrupted privacy statement, Regal built a "static node" the agent reads without being interrupted before handing callers back to a human agent.
Compliance was a key stakeholder from the start. "For any business that's regulated it's not a plug-and-play solution," said Atul Kumar, eHealth's VP of product and AI.

Meta announced a range of ad updates at its Advertising Week presentation in New York, including an improved business assistant, an expansion of its creative tools for brands and new shopping experiences.

Meta is beefing up its AI-powered business assistant, which provides conversational guidance on key ad creation elements, by adding new creative insights and giving it more memory and context: “the context of what you tried last quarter, your seasonality, and the goals you’ve described,” Meta said.

Meta is also testing importing tools that let brands upload their strategy and brand voice guidelines, adding agentic capacity so the assistant can generate creative, update targeting and change an ad's budget via conversational prompts, and testing scheduled tasks such as recurring performance reports and alerts.
Ads Creative Studio is expanding to more advertisers, the Meta Ads MCP server now supports more use cases for third-party AI tools, and Customer Lifecycle Strategy is available to all advertisers.

In Advantage+ creative, generating video from existing static assets is now generally available; Ads Creative Studio adds tools to change hooks, adjust audio and clip length, add text overlays and captions, or change end scenes.
Meta is working with Shopify on direct checkout via Meta Business Agent on Messenger, and testing similar checkout options for Meta AI with Adyen, PayPal, Shopify and Stripe.

Dentsu announced that its Carat media agency is partnering with NBC Universal, Freewheel and AI firm Newton to launch a planning, buying and optimization agent to use in upfront investments. Tinuiti launched a “Bliss Point Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server”, opening its measurement layer directly to AI agents. Stagwell relaunched its Assembly media agency as Stagwell Media, whose centerpiece is an agentic system called Machine OS.

But not every client is onboard with moving so fast, and the agencies' answer to fears of rogue agents is, almost always, human hand-holding. “Everything still requires human oversight,” said Rebekah Shalit, head of platforms at Dentsu. Freewheel's David Dworin said most agentic systems are designed with a human that has to approve everything, or very specific controls.

WPP Media's Lauren Wetzel said it requires “explicit controls, approval thresholds, accountable human oversight” where there's a financial or activation impact. Carat chief investment officer Carrie Drinkwater was more bullish: “If we don't start now, we'll be behind.”

From August 17, budget-limited Target CPA and Target ROAS campaigns that beat their targets are pulled back toward them; campaigns that overshoot on cost are left alone.

Mike Ryan's analysis of 383 million impressions found that by July 2026 roughly 29% of what advertisers bought as exact match was being broadened by AI Max. Other studies put AI Max at about 35% lower return on ad spend than traditional match types.

Google's own figures have moved: AI Max launched on May 6, 2025 with a claim of 14% more conversions or conversion value at similar cost. By the April 2026 general availability announcement the figure was 7%, on Google's internal 2026 data excluding retail. A holiday guide later used 15%, under a different definition.
Meanwhile Alphabet's Search revenue rose 17% to $63.27 billion in the second quarter. Advertisers, PPC Land concludes, increasingly have to judge results with instruments Google does not make.

For paid media marketers in healthcare, financial or legal fields, AI raises flags, from the black box of automated bidding to AI-generated creative. Know your company's policies and industry guidelines, and be careful what data you feed to AI tools.
AI Max's text customization can pull in ad copy that doesn't match approved messaging, and final URL expansion can link to unwanted pages. If you test AI Max, consider disabling both.

Brands don't expect ChatGPT ads to gift them significant sales this holiday season. Beyond expensive cost-per-click rates and unproven sales, AI assistants are still establishing themselves as a trustworthy source for product recommendations.

Sensor Tower data shows over 1,400 unique advertisers ran ads on ChatGPT in August, an 8% month-over-month increase, though most spend comes from large companies such as Capital One, Expedia and Cloudflare.

“Generally the results have been pretty bad,” said Measured's Terence Einhorn. “The equivalent to the cost-per-click on ChatGPT is around 6X of that on Google.” Superfiliate's Anders Bill said most brands aren't moving meaningful budgets away from Meta or search yet.
“Brands can't afford to use something until they know it works,” Einhorn added. “And they're not gonna know it works until they're using it.”
OpenAI is hiring a salesperson with a mandate to turn ChatGPT ads into a standing line item on agency media plans.

A listing for an Agency Partner on the company's Ads Solutions team calls for someone to drive advertiser revenue “through strategic relationships with leading agency holding companies.” The New York-based role pays a base salary of $216,000 to $273,000, plus equity and commission.

The hire will lead joint business planning with agencies, run agency education and enablement, and build relationships with senior agency staff across investment, strategy, planning, innovation, data, and commerce at both independent agencies and holding companies.
It is the same holding-company sales layer that Meta and Google use to lock in recurring spend.

As the artificial intelligence (AI) agent market grows quickly, commerce platforms are taking divergent positions. When an AI agent searches and pays on a user's behalf, the point of contact with the user becomes the AI agent rather than the platform.

Amazon recently blocked Meta's AI agent 'Muse', citing a violation of its terms of use, when it tried to search for and buy products on Amazon on users' behalf. Amazon argues that Meta did not obtain prior approval and that the agent did not clearly disclose that it was an AI. eBay also revised its terms in February to ban unauthorized access by third-party AI shopping agents.

Google, by contrast, unveiled an open commerce standard (UCP) with Shopify in January and began a pilot of direct purchases through Gemini in India. On the 6th, Meta, Walmart, Shopify, Stripe and others agreed to create a common standard for verifying AI agents' identities and the permissions delegated to them.

When AI agents take over searching, comparing and paying, users no longer pass through apps and search bars, weakening core platform assets such as ad exposure, recommendation algorithms, customer behavior data and membership lock-in. In Korea, Naver is restricting access by outside agents while expanding its own shopping AI agent features, and Coupang, the country's No. 1 e-commerce company, is also blocking outside AI from making payments in its app.

Integral Ad Science on September 30, 2026 extended its Low-Quality GenAI Avoidance product to YouTube, giving advertisers a way to keep campaigns away from mass-produced AI video. It is available globally through IAS's YouTube Optimization and Total Media Quality products, activated via an account representative. IAS says more "Social and Video platforms" will follow, without naming them.

Three components: AI slop becomes a category in Custom Brand Suitability profiles; Automated Avoidance excludes content before the bid "with automated daily refreshes"; and post-bid TMQ reporting includes AVOC rates. Classifications are built "using contextual signals from the YouTube Data API, and are not reviewed by Google."

The post gives no accuracy rate, languages, pricing or effect on reach, and does not mention Shorts or CTV. A Kapwing study found 21% of the first 500 Shorts shown to a new account were AI slop, with top slop channels earning an estimated $4 million to $4.25 million a year from ads.

A growing number of consumers say they feel an aversion to ads made with generative AI. They point out that the unnaturalness peculiar to AI images actually dampens their desire to buy. Lim Hyun-seo (28), who saw images of AI models wearing clothes on an online fashion platform, said, "I wonder how I'm supposed to trust AI images like these and buy clothes." On social media, reactions such as "The menu photos at the chicken place near my house are made with AI, and they give me the creeps every time I see them" have appeared.
Others criticized businesses that make AI ads to save money, saying their trust in them falls. Some also say they are tired of AI video ads shown repeatedly on YouTube and elsewhere.

Park Eun-a, a psychology professor at Daegu University, said "AI advertising is a question of authenticity," explaining that the more consumers perceive AI as heavily used in making an ad, the less authentic they find the ad. Lee Eun-hee, a consumer studies professor at Inha University, stressed that "using AI images to cut costs can actually be an act that lowers trust."

THG Commerce, part of THG Ingenuity, has integrated Criteo Sponsored Products into its AI Shopping Assistant, built using Google Cloud’s Gemini Enterprise. THG Commerce says it is the first commerce technology provider in Europe to bring Criteo Sponsored Products into AI powered conversational search.

The integration places sponsored and organic product recommendations side by side within the same conversation. Early results show sponsored products surfaced through the assistant reached a click-through rate more than five times the average, and a conversion rate more than double the average.

The assistant draws keywords and filters from each conversation and turns them into tailored product recommendations. Criteo’s relevance models, including keyword matching, semantic understanding and strict relevance thresholds, apply in the conversational context, so sponsored recommendations appear clearly labelled and only when they match what the shopper asked for.

“Customers start their shopping journey with a conversation... That is some of the highest-intent traffic a retailer can have, and until now it has largely sat outside retail media,” said Darren Rajanah, Chief Revenue Officer, THG Ingenuity.

Inference fleets face a capacity paradox: they can be globally constrained while meaningful pockets of capacity remain locally idle. Meta built a system that aggregates these pockets into a shared opportunistic capacity pool and turns them into better ads recommendations, without requiring additional capacity orders.

The capacity may be reclaimed with little notice, so Meta uses two elasticity levers. Rank More Ads (RMA) adjusts the number of candidates evaluated by the ranking stages. Serve Better Models (SBM) adjusts the share of requests routed to a more powerful model.

RMA requires both CPU and accelerator capacity, while SBM can use accelerator-only surplus. Physical and logical isolation protects baseline serving; a PID controller tunes candidate volume from tail latency, and value-aware load shedding at servers and clients reacts within milliseconds when capacity is reclaimed.
Next, Meta is extending both levers, developing precomputation elasticity, expanding cross-region inference, and building an optimization-based system to allocate AI inference capacity automatically.

Meta on September 29, 2026 extended Muse, the personal AI agent it released three weeks earlier, into a product for small businesses in the US and Canada. Muse for Small Business adds connectors to 15 third-party tools including Shopify, Intuit QuickBooks, Klaviyo, Stripe and Canva, alongside Facebook Pages, Instagram professional account analytics and Meta ad accounts. Meta says "nothing publishes, sends, or spends without your approval."

For advertisers, the significant line is the one about ad accounts. Earlier integrations — the ads MCP server opened to Claude and ChatGPT in April — required bringing an external model to Meta's interfaces. Here the model, the agent, the app and the ad account all belong to Meta. The post does not say whether ad-account access is read-only or can change budgets, bids or creative, nor whether connector data is kept out of Meta's ad systems.

The only quantified outcome is one tester's: grocer Tom Mulholland says Muse cut at least 15 minutes from payroll. Muse is free for most uses, with subscription plans whose prices Meta has not stated. Meta's Q2 2026 revenue was $60.80 billion, more than 97% of it from ads.

American Express is introducing a framework designed to capture and authenticate a customer’s purchase intent before an AI agent completes the transaction. Dubbed the “Intent Intelligence Framework,” the company hopes it will become an industry standard for AI-powered transactions.

It starts with a Create Intent API that captures the customer’s purchase instructions and constraints, like the merchant’s name and maximum budget. The customer authenticates and signs off, then an Intent ID and a Proof of Intent Token are created. The token is used to obtain a secure payment credential the agent uses at checkout instead of the actual card number.

“Our approach differs from the implementations of others in that it pulls intent earlier into the transaction flow,” said Hannah Bozian, Amex’s VP of Agentic Partnerships and Strategy. If a customer asks for white Nike sneakers in size 9 but the agent tries to buy Adidas, Amex could stop the transaction.
Amex said it has not yet seen more disputes from agentic commerce. The framework joins its ACE Developer Toolkit, launched in April.

blocks.cap: Salesforce plugs Koa, trained on 27 years of CRM simulations, in beside Claude and ChatGPT

blocks.x: Salesforce published an interview in which Chief Data Officer Michael Andrew argued that customers should be able to switch between frontier, open and custom AI models, including Koa, the company’s first CRM reasoning model, which it says was built with NVIDIA and trained in simulations drawn from 27 years of running CRM workflows.
Koa is “orchestrated alongside frontier models rather than in place of them.” The page gives no parameter count, benchmark score, price or availability date.

“Different models have different strengths and weaknesses, and they’re changing all the time,” Andrew said. “AI is a fuel… we want to let that fuel come from anywhere, whether it’s Anthropic and Claude, OpenAI and ChatGPT.”

The choice message lands six weeks after the Claudeforce partnership made Claude the default model for Slack and several Agentforce surfaces. For marketers, the model behind a CRM agent shapes response time, reliability and consumption costs.

blocks.cap: Bannerflow heatmaps predict ad attention before spend, with zero validation data behind the scores

blocks.x: Bannerflow put a name on the AI tools in its creative platform. The suite, Creative Intelligence, groups image generation, predictive attention scoring, a performance analysis layer and feed-driven dynamic ads into four stages: Create, Evaluate, Understand and Act and scale.

Predictive scoring uses “attention heatmaps, focus analysis and clarity scoring” to indicate how a creative “is likely to capture attention before campaign budget is committed,” and flags distracting elements. Creative Insights relates elements such as calls to action, colour and animation timing to performance. Teams can also generate, expand and upscale images and set up product feeds in plain language.

The release gives no availability dates, no pricing and no validation data for its predictive models. “Marketing teams have more performance data than ever, but too little of it inspires the next piece of creative,” said Chief Product Officer Moses Velasco.

blocks.cap: John Keeble via Getty Images

blocks.x: Google is testing ads for branded prescription drugs in AI Mode and AI Overviews, opening its AI search platform to one of the most tightly regulated categories in advertising, the company confirmed to ADWEEK.

The testing for pharmaceutical products, including prescription drugs, began this month and is limited to the U.S, according to a Google spokesperson. Pharmaceutical advertisers can run standard text and Shopping ads, which will appear in sections labeled as “Sponsored.”
“We’re testing standard text and Shopping ads in AI Mode and AI Overviews, which we recently expanded to include certain pharmaceutical products,” a Google spokesperson said in a statement.

Magnite and LG Ad Solutions announced LG smart TV home screen inventory will be available to agencies through agentic AI media buying. Northern California Toyota Dealers Association is part of the first campaign, with indie agency H/L, featuring 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy in a split-screen hero placement.

H/L's buyer agent collaborated with Magnite's seller agent within ClearLine via Model Context Protocol (MCP). The agents set up and activated the campaign brief for NFL viewers in market for a new car, and the agent-led plan was approved by LG and H/L before it went live.

Home screen ads have become "table stakes," said Jeremy Cobb, VP at H/L. Agentic buying "is not something that's going to fundamentally change what we're doing," he said, but he expects it to make campaign planning better, faster and stronger.

Bill Hunt audited 122 leading Shopify storefronts to test whether an agent can actually resolve a purchase decision. Shopify switched on agent tools for every store: 89 of 122 answered a standard MCP tool listing, and checkout creation succeeded on every store given a real, in-stock item.
But every one of the 74 checkouts returned requires_escalation: the agent builds a priced cart, and a person commits the money.

Policy tools answered return-window questions but failed buyer-style questions on shipping and cancellation. None of 74 stores returned an arrival estimate, no store declared pickup, and not one of 122 exposes a tool to cancel, change or return an order. Across nine checks, zero stores passed.
Hunt's advice: ask your own policy tool the questions buyers ask, and verify rather than assume you are "agent-ready."

blocks.cap: Floqer founders

blocks.x: Floqer is an autonomous customer knowledge platform that gives B2B sales and marketing teams an AI-powered database that continuously collects, organizes and updates customer information. Pitching at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026's Startup Battlefield, it plans to open-source the technology, targeting early 2027 pending security reviews.

Users describe what they are looking for, and its AI agents search across sources to build lists of companies and contacts, enrich accounts from more than 100 third-party data sources, and monitor the web for job changes or new funding. Customers have reported cutting prospecting time by as much as 70%, the company says.
Founded in 2024 by Shivam Mahajan and Zaaheda Islam, Floqer says it has passed $1.2 million in ARR, has eight employees and more than 1,000 customers, including Perplexity, Wise and AngelList.

Newegg has integrated Google's Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) for online checkout, following Wayfair, Walmart, Macy's and others that have supported UCP since Google launched it in January. Newegg-sold products will be purchasable within Google's AI Mode, Google Search and Gemini.

"AI is changing how the world buys technology, and Newegg intends to be at the forefront of that change," said Montaque Hou, chief information officer at Newegg. Newegg remains the merchant of record while providing Google with product catalog data.
The move follows Celeste, Newegg's own conversational AI assistant, and support for listings in Perplexity's search. Shoppers can use Google Pay without leaving their search results or prompts.
"Newegg enabling UCP-powered checkout on Google marks a new milestone as we scale agentic commerce," said Ashish Gupta of Google.

blocks.cap: Shopify previously announced a partnership with Meta’s Muse for AI-powered shopping and checkout.

blocks.x: More AI agents will soon be able to browse and purchase from Shopify listings, marking an expansion of the company’s agentic commerce ambitions.

Shopify announced Tuesday it will let shoppers configure their AI agents to purchase products on their behalf, giving more agents access to over a billion listings in Shopify’s catalog, which includes items on and off Shopify storefronts. In September, Shopify partnered with Meta to let its Muse agent buy on a human’s behalf; now, shoppers can use any agent without a partnership integration.

Customers connect an agent to their account on Shop and check out within the conversation using one-click Shop Pay. Orders are funneled back to the Shop app. Shopify markets the feature as a “personal shopper” that can follow rules like budget guardrails or fast shipping only. Buyers must approve each purchase.

E-commerce has become one of the battlegrounds of AI, with Google and Amazon investing in agent shopping tools, and Amazon fighting Perplexity and, more recently, Meta’s Muse over whether agents should shop on a customer’s behalf.

Google said Universal Cart, a tool that lets users collect and monitor products they find across Search and in the Gemini app, is now available to U.S. users. It was first previewed at Google I/O in May.

The cart can collect items from multiple retailers and send notifications when a saved product's price drops or an out-of-stock item is back. Google says it can also factor in credit card perks and surface relevant promo codes.

Checkout is tied to Google's Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), an open standard designed to help AI agents and retailers work together across the shopping journey. Amazon, OpenAI and other rivals have added agentic commerce features too.

blocks.cap: Jeff Collins, Fox ad sales chief, during the 2025 Fox upfront presentation. Frank Micelotta/Fox

blocks.x: Fox is expanding what it calls the TV ad industry's “first end-to-end agentic platform” as it continues its push into AI-powered technology.

The company told ADWEEK it is entering the next phase of its agentic rollout: adding more agency partners, expanding agentic capabilities to end-to-end linear and, eventually, digital transactions, and making agentic a bigger part of future upfront conversations.
According to Jeff Collins, Fox's ads leader, the tech advancements are creating more impactful relationships with clients and partners.
Google Ads seems to be testing a new report named the Search terms and ad combinations report. It shows how search queries, ad creatives and landing pages work together.
It was spotted by Natasha Kaurra, who said on LinkedIn it “looks like a useful addition for advertisers running AI Max for Search campaigns.”

blocks.cap: Google Ads Search Terms And Ad Combinations Report

blocks.x: Beyond the search terms that triggered ads, it shows the headlines and descriptions served, the landing pages users were sent to, match sources (AI Max expanded matches or landing page and URL inclusions) and asset sources (whether assets were advertiser-provided).
“This report gives us another way to identify mismatches between search intent, ad messaging, and landing pages,” Kaurra added.

blocks.cap: Stripe President John Collison. Getty Images Entertainment via Getty Images

blocks.x: Stripe President John Collison said on his Cheeky Pint podcast, speaking with Meta Platforms CEO Mark Zuckerberg and chief AI officer Alexandr Wang, that agentic commerce on Stripe rose sharply starting in September.
“…we had a whole bunch of announcements at Sessions back in May, and then it only, as of September, basically started going vertical,” Collison said. He gave no specific figures.

The remark came as the three discussed Meta's AI assistant Muse and its ability to buy merchandise on command. Amazon recently banned Muse from shopping on its site; Zuckerberg said companies that block it will likely regret it.

Meta published a technical account of the 2026 generation of its Generative Ads Model, GEM, claiming an 18.9% conversion improvement and a 12% click-through rate improvement across its ad surfaces and objectives. The company replaced separate prediction systems for Facebook, Instagram and Reels with one central foundation model, whose output is moved into the hundreds of smaller models that serve ads in real time.
The post does not say what the figures are measured against, over what period, or whether they come from A/B tests or offline evaluation. They are vendor-supplied and not independently audited.

A new architecture, Kunlun, replaces Interformer and "delivers 2x performance gains with the same computation scaling," according to Meta. LoopFM and Solaris pass GEM's knowledge to downstream models, and GEM trains "on several thousand of the latest-generation GPUs" at 20-25% MFU.
For advertisers, none of these mechanisms has a setting in Ads Manager; their effects arrive through Advantage+ and automated delivery.
Google is starting to test ads in AI Mode in Search for users who connect their apps through Personal Intelligence, reversing its earlier ad-free approach to the experience.

The update means Google may now use insights from connected apps to help personalize ads, alongside the information already used to generate AI-powered responses. Ads will continue to reflect the user's query, the context of the AI-generated response and their interests.

Google says protections remain: connecting apps is opt-in, ads will not be based directly on the contents of Gmail or Google Photos, advertisers cannot access connected apps, and sensitive information will not be used to personalize ads.
Google has not announced new advertiser controls, targeting options or a wider rollout for this test.

OpenAI is rolling out several updates to ChatGPT Ads, including expanded measurement partnerships, improved conversion reporting, weekly performance summaries and experiments with larger, more visual ad formats.

New measurement integrations include Northbeam, DV Rockerbox and INCRMNTAL, alongside mobile measurement partners Kochava, Tenjin and Airbridge. A redesigned Conversions page in Ads Manager brings together conversion activity, event trends, optimization status and diagnostic warnings.

Tests include wider ad cards and larger images on desktop and full-width images on mobile, using advertisers' existing creative. Separately, OpenAI plans to test a multi-image ad format during image generation, initially with selected U.S. advertisers.
OpenAI has not shared performance results or confirmed a broader rollout timeline for these formats.

blocks.cap: Image: Sipa USA via AP.

blocks.x: OpenAI lets anyone inject ads into ChatGPT users' sessions, targeting specific groups of people based on their email address, phone number, or a unique identifier on their phone, according to 404 Media's own tests of ChatGPT's advertising ecosystem.

While the ad targeting available in ChatGPT is somewhat standard practice across the advertising industry, the chatbot's one billion monthly active users may not understand they, in some cases, are being specifically targeted because of their personal data the advertiser has uploaded to OpenAI. ChatGPT's ad targeting is also novel in that it is also based on the prompts users enter into the chatbot, prompts that users may assume are private but which, as 404 Media has previously shown, may be reviewed by humans. Or in this case, used for ad targeting purposes.

blocks.cap: Thrad doubles in-chat ad spend for AI apps to $1m, pictured as a coin dropped into a chat bubble

blocks.x: Thrad, a San Francisco company that places sponsored messages inside AI chat conversations, opened Monetization Fund II, a rolling program that directs up to $1 million in advertiser spend through its DSP to consumer AI apps willing to test ads. No equity changes hands and no cash grant is paid out.
It doubles the $500,000 first round from December 2025. The announcement does not state the revenue share, per-app allocation or how long the program runs.
"Many users simply won't pay for a subscription," said CEO Andrea Tortella, pointing to the token costs behind every interaction.
Ads are matched to what the conversation is about rather than to a user profile, and run as native sponsored placements with "clear disclosure" to separate them from the AI's organic responses.

blocks.cap: Meta flips product browsing on in live ads October 28, citing 3% more conversions; opt-out available

blocks.x: Meta has notified advertisers that, starting October 28, 2026, it will add product browsing to ads already running on Facebook and Instagram unless they opt out before that date. When people tap an ad, they may see an in-app experience with product info and personalized suggestions instead of going straight to the advertiser's website.

Meta says businesses saw 3% more conversions on average, based on an experiment run August 6–21, 2026 across about 117,700 advertisers. The notice does not define the conversion metric, the comparison group or cost per conversion.

Advertisers can opt out via the notice or toggle the feature in each ad's Advantage+ Creative and Destination settings. Media buyer David Herrmann, who called it an AI feature that turns creatives into dynamic product ads, objected to the timing just before the holiday season.

blocks.x: ChatGPT-attributed sessions in GA4 fell by 22% to 57% from Oct. 9 for sites tracked by Graphite, CEO Ethan Smith said, roughly a 45% fall from baseline. LLM Pulse saw about 46% fewer ChatGPT sessions on Oct. 9–11 while total traffic held steady.

Smith says ChatGPT began opening links in answer text without the utm_source=chatgpt.com tag or a referrer, so those visits can appear as Direct. There is not enough data yet to tell whether some visits were also lost.

Adobe’s Cedric Huesler found ChatGPT visits on about 500 pages fell by about 31,000 a day while Direct rose by about 26,000. Profound tied it to ChatGPT’s new Intelligent UI answer format after the GPT-6 rollout.

Huesler says OpenAI confirmed on Oct. 14 it was a bug and a fix began rolling out Oct. 15; Profound says it hasn’t seen official word. Smith and Huesler suggest annotating Oct. 8–15 in reporting and comparing ChatGPT and Direct traffic side by side.

Last month, VideoAmp, Comscore and iSpot received re-certifications from the US Joint Industry Committee. Still, buyers and sellers aren’t ready to ditch Nielsen, so alternative currency companies are focusing on data and measurement more broadly.

Over the summer, VideoAmp cut about 20% of its headcount as part of an effort to entrust more operations to AI. SVP Andrea Zapata said the goal is to use AI to help media buyers plan smarter campaigns that perform better against their intended outcomes.

One top priority is to connect its planning and measurement workflows with AI agents, said chief product officer Josh Hudgins. Agents can help buyers optimize campaigns in-flight — for example, cutting spend on one inventory source and buying inventory that efficiently adds unique reach.
AI still needs first-party viewer data, via clean rooms and publishers’ log-level data, plus ACR data. “Ultimately, what we’re all trying to get is outcomes,” Zapata said.
On Google’s Ads Decoded podcast on October 15, Google Ads product manager Tal Akabas said changing the target or budget of an established campaign does not put it into a learning period.

“When you change your target or your budget, there isn’t actually a learning period,” Akabas said. “The Google Ads back end system will scale bids directly in proportion to your target changes.” For a net new campaign without prior information, “some learning period can take place.”
The claim is narrow: it covers target and budget edits on steady campaigns, not new assets, targeting or bid strategies.

The episode also gave rollout status: promotion mode is leaving beta on Search and PMax, a reporting-only mode for new customers is rolling out, and re-engagement only mode is launching in Performance Max, with Search and Shopping to follow.
Brands can’t tell ChatGPT how to talk about their products, but they can invest in more branded content to give the models beneath chatbots more to work with.

Fender overhauled its website into a “front door” for storytelling, with short videos on its heritage and artists like Jimi Hendrix, partly to improve visibility during product research. Seven out of 10 U.S. consumers use ChatGPT or AI summaries when researching products, per a Skyword survey.

Marshall, whose amps Hendrix played through, is pushing its ‘Dead Venues’ YouTube series. “It’s such an important place for us to show up,” said vp Christine Kennedy Grant of AI Overviews and LLM tools.
“ChatGPT is the new word of mouth,” said Attention Arc’s Urvashi Manral. Three-fourths (75%) of marketers plan to increase spending on visibility in AI assistants next year, according to Kantar.

Meta's updated Commercial Terms, which take effect Oct. 30, give the company permission to crawl websites associated with businesses that use its products and to use that content to train those products. The terms apply to any business use of Meta's products, from running ads to managing a Facebook Page.

Nieman Lab reported that three legal professionals believe the language could support an argument that Meta may scrape news sites to train its AI products. Meta spokesperson Andy Stone called that summary false, saying the update is about pulling accurate product information and is "not about scraping news sites."

Meta's ad terms already let it crawl advertisers' websites for uses that include training. The October version reaches businesses that don't buy ads. The clause also lets Meta "create test credentials" to reach those pages.

Meta says content owners can still manage access with robots.txt, but neither updated terms mention it. Site owners can block Meta-ExternalAgent, its AI training crawler, while allowing Meta-WebIndexer.

blocks.x: The National Trust has suspended all advertising on TikTok after a run of AI-generated promotional videos appeared without the charity's approval. According to the charity, the adverts were created in error by TikTok Ads and were never meant to go live.

In a statement on LinkedIn, the Trust said it had paused its TikTok activity while it investigated. A spokesperson told Civil Society it was working directly with TikTok to understand the incident and put extra safeguards in place.

Marketers said the AI-made videos sat awkwardly beside the Trust's established identity. Charlotte Anstee of Ocean said local social media teams had previously been told there was an AI ban. Alex Pollard of Pollard Media noted the charity's extensive image archive.

Harri Brown, co-founder of Antler Social, said advertisers can avoid unexpected AI assets by disabling the setting that automatically adds newly generated material during delivery, and remove any already inserted manually.

Meta now offers 15 always-on standard topics in Reels Trending Ads, the format that places an ad immediately after the most-watched and most culturally relevant Reels on Facebook and Instagram. New categories include Home & Garden and Spanish-language content.

Meta announced the update at its Brand Building Summit on 16 October. Advertisers can also choose seasonal lineups built around the holidays and the start of the football and basketball seasons. Custom audience exclusions arrive later this year, letting a campaign leave chosen custom audiences out.

Meta says campaigns that included Reels Trending Ads increased action intent by more than 5 percentage points against control groups, with an incremental 5 percentage point lift in unaided brand awareness. Both figures are Meta's own.

Meta opened the format to all advertisers globally in September 2025, saying it uses AI to place ads directly after top-trending, creator-generated Reels. The approach is close to TikTok's Pulse family. Reels make up more than half of all time spent on Instagram, according to the company.

Demandbase said on October 15, 2026, that Salesforce has named it a launch data partner for Hunter, the outbound sales agent Salesforce is still piloting. Hunter users get Demandbase engagement, person, account, buying group and intent data inside Salesforce "with no additional contracts required for the data within Salesforce."

The integration uses the Demandbase MCP server, so sales reps can prompt Demandbase in natural language within Agentforce to identify and prioritize the most engaged prospects. "Sales teams can only act on the signals they can see," said Salesforce VP of Product Management Rohan Punamia.

"Hunter is currently in pilot, with general availability planned later this year," the release says, with no month given. It gives no price for Hunter, no data scope, and no statement on exclusivity. "No additional contracts" is also not the same as "no additional cost."

blocks.cap: Dado Ruvic/Reuters

blocks.x: This coming holiday season, brands will have a new type of shopper to court: AI agents.

Cheq, a cybersecurity company that verifies AI shopping agents, says it recorded a 100x surge in agentic traffic over a 45-day period following the release of consumer AI agents like Instinct and Meta's Muse. While agents still make up a small fraction of online shoppers, they're growing quickly, especially among a constant drumbeat of consumer agent releases, Cheq CEO Guy Tytunovich said.
But not everyone is on board: Amazon and eBay have blocked agents to reinforce control over their ads businesses and checkout experiences.

blocks.cap: A chart showing how likely US adults are to use AI to shop.

blocks.x: Consumers are hesitant, too. Shoppers are now as likely to be swayed by an agent's recommendation as by an influencer, Morning Consult finds, but few are comfortable letting AI make purchases on their behalf. This holiday season will be the first true test of which brands are best at displaying their wares in ways that agents find irresistible.

blocks.x: Meta recently updated its commercial terms of use, declaring that the company can “use any content from [a business account’s] domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of” Meta products and services.

According to legal experts interviewed by Nieman Lab, this looked like a “remarkable provision” that could give Meta permission to scrape the website of any publisher with a Meta business account and use the content to train the company’s AI models. (While Meta defeated a high-profile lawsuit over alleged copyright infringement last year, other cases against AI companies, including Meta, continue.)
However, a Meta spokesperson insisted that the updated terms did not reflect a change in the way Meta crawls the web. And now, The Verge reports that the provision has been removed.

“We’ve heard you and want to clarify: the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves,” the company said in a statement. “It does not change how Meta uses web crawlers.”

blocks.cap: monday.com’s Harmony AI caller hands warm leads to reps, which one car broker says lifted deals 9%

blocks.x: monday.com began selling Harmony on October 19, 2026: a voice AI platform whose agents place and answer sales calls for mid-market and enterprise companies, qualify leads and hand the promising ones live to human reps.

The agents run on voice technology acquired from OneAI and a set of proprietary, task-specific small LLMs, with dialing and CRM write-back built on Twilio. The company claims about 200ms audio-in to audio-out latency and “a contact rate of up to 70%,” without a baseline or method.

The only named customer, UK broker Bright Car Finance, says the agent follows up every approved applicant at once, qualifies about half its conversations, hands 80% of those to advisers and drove a 9% rise in deals closed in less than a year. PPC Land notes it is unclear whether that is relative or percentage points.
Harmony is available in the US, UK, Australia and Singapore. No pricing, error rates or independent testing were published.

Minerva CEO Jackson Engles admits the data his startup is built on probably isn’t a durable moat, even after raising $20 million to build AI agents for marketers on an identity graph of 270 million consumers. His answer is to stay narrow: “Marketers shouldn’t just be using Claude and bringing in random data.”

A brand plugs its CRM, warehouse and other sources into Minerva, where an “agentic data engineer” built with OpenAI maps them. Agents then unify the data into one view per customer and enrich it from Minerva’s “B2B2C identity graph.” Ramp used the work-to-personal link to extend direct mail and lifted its MQL rate around 80% in three months; Wander saw 3.4x ROAS on Meta lookalikes versus broad targeting, per Engles.

A second agent, an “agentic data scientist,” would build predictive models from plain-language requests. Minerva calls the layer an agentic CDP internally but doesn’t market it that way: customers “want the outcome of a CDP.”

blocks.cap: ChatGPT at 74.5%, Claude at 72.3%: a balance scale nearly level as marketers split their AI tools

blocks.x: Basis’s fourth annual “AI and the Future of Marketing” report surveyed 184 marketing and advertising professionals from July 16 to August 14, 2026. ChatGPT use fell to 74.5% from 88.6%, while Claude rose to 72.3% from 17.9%; Copilot is at 55.4% and Gemini at 47.8%.

Daily AI use reached 61.4%, up from 33.6%. The share of organizations running AI agents rose from 20.0% to 51.1%, mostly for reporting and analytics (72.3%) and campaign briefs (56.4%); media buying is the least delegated at 18.1%.

Only 6.5% measure AI ROI with defined metrics and benchmarks; 23.4% measure it anecdotally. PPC Land notes the small sample, undisclosed recruitment, and that Basis sells the unified platform its conclusions recommend.

Measuring how chatbots shape brand discovery is mostly still a mystery. But “you can’t improve what you can’t measure,” said Michael McCash, GM of growth at Australian home loan and property sales company Lendi Group.

McCash built an in-house multi-touch attribution model for Lendi’s more than $10 million in annual paid media and brought in Mutinex for MMM, which showed free-to-air TV was underweighted. Lendi is also a pilot customer of Mutinex’s AI Visibility tool, which mass-prompts LLMs and analyzes how brands surface, and uses Tracksuit and Askable for brand tracking and surveys.

Ads inside chatbots such as ChatGPT and Gemini haven’t been major ROI contributors yet: CPMs and acquisition rates are too high. What Lendi does see is a more informed customer arriving further down the funnel after researching with LLMs, so for now its AI investment goes to measurement rather than chatbot ads.

Amazon retired the "Amazon DSP" name at unBoxed 2026 but kept the buying engine, moving the controls traders use behind an advanced-settings toggle, according to an October 1 analysis by the trade newsletter ADOTAT. The column argues Amazon's AI agent now chooses channels, audiences and bids in its default path, then grades the results with Amazon's own data. Amazon says the DSP's programmatic capabilities remain available within DVA+ advanced settings.

Under the new Amazon Ads Agent umbrella sit Sponsored Ads, DVA+ and Full-Funnel Campaigns. In Full-Funnel, which starts at $100 a day, Amazon allocates the budget across formats toward outcomes such as new-to-brand sales. "The thing that is actually live for U.S. advertisers, subject to eligibility, is Full-Funnel Campaigns," ADOTAT wrote. "The thing that keeps the trader's hands on the wheel is the thing still in beta." DVA+ was in US closed beta, with open beta expected in late October.
"Defaults are destiny," the column states. ADOTAT labels its commercial reading as inference, and its free preview does not say Full-Funnel blocks audience selection.

Google says tens of millions of small business owners already use Gemini to brainstorm products, manage customer feedback and analyze performance. It is now launching a dedicated business landing page: a central hub to build a brand, analyze finances and understand customer insights.
Gemini can connect to Google Business Profile, Google Ads and Google Workspace, plus third-party apps including Adobe, Canva, Dropbox, Shopify, Wix, Zoho and Xero.

For on-brand visuals, businesses can upload their website, brand kit, fonts or color palettes. Paired with Nano Banana 2.1, Google's latest image model, Gemini delivers end-to-end visuals for product launches or ongoing campaigns and retains the style so owners don't have to re-upload guidelines.

Gemini can also turn messy spreadsheets, receipts and purchase records into financial graphics and interactive models. Google highlights owners such as a ceramicist in Bordeaux who saves two to three hours a day on product descriptions and social posts.
The landing page, marketing and finance skills and new connected apps begin rolling out globally to all Gemini app users in the coming days.

A study released Tuesday by supply chain intelligence firm DecryptAds uncovered more than 2,100 AI-generated recipe sites following the made-for-advertising (MFA) playbook: overlapping ad placements on low-effort pages. Ads from major blue-chip and Fortune 500 brands appeared on them.

The sites feature fabricated authors whose “about” pages use AI-generated avatars, stock images, stolen photos of real chefs or even altered images of celebrities such as Emily Blunt. That runs afoul of a Google Search update this month calling fabricated creator profiles a form of deception.

Meta's Generative Recommenders (GenRecs) shift its ads system from scoring every ad candidate to using LLM architecture to reason about ad content and user preferences together. The foundation is GenRecs Tokenization: instead of a dedicated ID for every item, each ad, product, page or pixel is represented by tokens from a stable semantic vocabulary.

Pre-trained multimodal models read an item's text and images into an embedding; the tokenizer combines that with engagement-learned representations and quantizes the result into a short sequence of discrete tokens. The pipeline encodes, decomposes the embedding into subspaces, and maps each to a codebook entry. Similar items share tokens, so a new trail shoe inherits what the model learned from last season's.
Across eight tokenizer versions, intrinsic measures (cluster purity, distribution balance, codebook utilization) correlated strongly with CTR prediction accuracy.
Better predictions for low-impression tail ads also improve training data for all ads, a self-reinforcing flywheel.

Paired with Meta's GEM and Adaptive Ranking Model, GenRecs Tokenization delivered a +0.35% lift in conversions across surfaces (Meta internal data, February 2026). Next: wider tokenization coverage and a shared token space across text, image, audio and video.

Walmart Connect's Ryan Mayward said conversations reveal more than keywords: "The opportunity is to be relevant to what a customer is trying to accomplish, not just what they're searching for." Marketplace SVP Manish Joneja said accurate product information, prices and delivery promises become even more important for AI-powered shopping.

OpenAI announced on Wednesday that ChatGPT Ads will expand into 26 new countries. Fourteen of them are in Latin America, including Argentina, Chile and Colombia. OpenAI also said more than 100,000 advertisers have run ads on the platform in the roughly eight months since launch.

That is not the same as 100,000 active advertisers: The Information reported about 60,000 active advertisers as of early October, citing New Street Research. OpenAI has shared how its ChatGPT advertising system interprets conversations, selects relevant ads, and keeps ad serving separate from organic answers. It says ChatGPT Ads reached $1 billion in annualized revenue run rate less than 200 days after launch, and more than 100,000 advertisers have run ads.
The system choosing ads runs separately from the one writing ChatGPT's answers, with its own models and code. ChatGPT doesn't wait for it; an ad that arrives too late won't appear with that response.
A model OpenAI calls the "orchestrator" reads the conversation, turns relevant parts into search queries and embeddings, and keeps track of details across "stateful" sessions.

It checks eligibility (location targeting, policy, budget, pacing), assesses fit and likely view, click or conversion, then sends candidates to a separate auction tool that handles final ranking, pricing and selection. The language model doesn't directly choose the winner or set the price.
Even an auction winner can be dropped by a post-auction fit check or miss the delivery window. The post gives no CPA, ROAS or conversion-rate benchmarks.

Plenty about CNN's future is up in the air now the Skydance deal has gone through. CNN International's plan to sell ads through AI agents isn't among them. Seven months after announcing the move, the network still has it on course to launch in the first quarter of 2027.
"I gave a Q1 timeline to have the first dollars flowing, which I would still be hopeful for," said Faisal Karmali, vp of digital operations for CNN International Commercial and Warner Bros Discovery.

The broadcaster is pairing its own agent infrastructure with outside technology partners such as demand-side platforms, which means teaching an agent its business rules, giving it a front end and making sure its inventory reads correctly to the LLMs buyers' agents rely on.

Open questions remain: what guardrails stop agents circumventing trading practices, and which vocabulary they use given competing standards. "Seller agents are a genuine efficiency gain for direct sales," said SWYM CEO Ravi Patel. "But they automate the deal, not the delivery."
Karmali called it "too early to say" whether agents could shift power to publishers. Agent-led deals could start at 5% of CNN International's ad business, he said, or one day reach 50%.

According to a new Feedvisor survey, ChatGPT is where 16% of shoppers start looking for products, but only 9% go there to buy. When an AI assistant recommends a product, only 5% buy it on the spot; the rest check platforms like Google and Amazon first for better prices.

PartnerCentric's findings show that after an AI suggestion, 33% of shoppers check existing reviews, 22.3% compare prices and 18.8% search Amazon or another retailer. Only 14.8% visit the brand's website. "AI is a starting point, not a final verdict," said founder and CEO Stephanie Harris.

Channel V Media's Kieran Powell said AI is winning the research step. A Prosper Insights & Analytics survey found only 7.3% would let an AI agent buy apparel. "If people won't let AI buy a $40 shirt for them, they won't let it tell them which shirt is good," Powell said.

Musely, which sees steadily growing traffic from AI assistants, is focused on GEO. "For us, the goal isn't simply to be mentioned by AI," said Paris Roche. Harris added: "When those signals conflict, AI does not smooth it over. It surfaces the gap sooner."

Lee Jung-heon, a lawmaker from the Democratic Party of Korea, pointed out that the generative AI ad-production platform of the Korea Broadcast Advertising Corporation (KOBACO) is failing to properly filter out illegal and harmful ads.

At the National Assembly Science, ICT, Broadcasting and Communications Committee's parliamentary audit on the 22nd, Lee entered keywords such as 'slot games that make money' and 'slot machines' into 'AiSAC', KOBACO's AI ad creation support platform, and actually produced an ad storyboard promoting illegal gambling games.
Lee said, "It should not just block specific words or images," adding, "It has to verify the full context and purpose of an ad as well."

Eom Jeong-hwan, acting president of KOBACO, said, "We started with good intentions, but because the filtering was centered on banned words and keywords, we did not manage to cover workarounds," adding, "We will strengthen filtering with an approach that grasps the full context and prepare a procedure that verifies once more at the final stage."
